tool.description: Create or update one entity and optional relationships. Use for KB mutations after validating intent; prefer a dryRun:true call first because it validates without writing and returns semantic advisor receipts for prose-heavy requirements. Use kb_model (mode requirement) before hand-writing strict property facts from prose, and kb_model (mode predicates) before hand-writing ontology predicate facts. Use the `relationships` array for batch creation of multiple links in a single call (e.g., linking a requirement to multiple tests or facts). An update keeps the properties and relationships it leaves out: send the fields that change (with title and status) and only the links to add. Prefer modeling requirements as reusable fact links (`constrains`, `requires_property`, or `requires_predicate`) so consistency and contradiction checks remain queryable. Relationship endpoints must already exist in KB. For requirements, the write will be rejected if it contradicts existing current requirements that constrain the same subject with incompatible properties. To replace a conflicting requirement, include a `supersedes` relationship from the new requirement to the old one in the same request, then upsert the old requirement with status closed (kb_check blocks a superseded requirement that is not closed). Successful writes may return non-blocking semantic advisor warnings; inspect and repair those warnings before treating prose as contradiction-checkable. For a requirement send the statement as `document.body` and the reason as `why`; give other entities a prose body (kb_check blocks one without context). Never invent a reason: write 'Reason not stated'. A requirement write returns its open kb_check steps as nextActions. Do not use for read-only inspection. Side effects: writes KB, may refresh symbol coordinates; dryRun:true writes nothing.

document.description: Optional source document write; omit body on update to keep it. New requirements take statement, Context, Source.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview without writing the KB or workspace; use it as the preflight before the real write.

id.description: Unique entity ID named by the behavior it governs (<TYPE>-<area>-<behavior>); an existing ID updates the entity.

implementedBy.description: req only: the declarations that implement it, each {sourceFile, symbol}; Kibi links each with implements.

plannedFacts.description: dryRun only: fact payloads (e.g. kb_model applyPlan entries) staged before this one, so their links resolve.

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).

properties.description: Entity fields to persist; must include title and status.

aliases.description: Optional vocabulary aliases for predicate discovery.

approval_ref.description: Requirement-only. Optional reference to the exception's approval decision record.

approved_by.description: Requirement-only: the human who approved this exception requirement.

argument_aliases.description: predicate_schema only: legacy spellings keyed by argument name, each mapped to a declared constant.

argument_constants.description: predicate_schema only: allowed constants keyed by argument name; unlisted arguments stay open.

argument_names.description: Ordered argument role names for predicate_schema facts.

argument_types.description: Ordered argument types for predicate_schema facts.

canonical_key.description: Optional canonical identity key for predicate or strict fact claims.

case_waiver.description: Fact-only: why the edge cases derived from this fact are covered elsewhere or cannot occur.

case_waiver_approved_by.description: Fact-only. The person who accepted case_waiver.

claim_key.description: Optional key of the clause this fact grounds; Kibi derives it from claim_text, and a sent key must match.

claim_text.description: Exact atomic requirement clause this fact represents; Kibi derives claim_key from it on a grounding fact.

closed_world.description: Optional closed-world marker for strict fact interpretation.

dimension_waiver.description: Fact-only: why the quantifier in claim_text ranges over nothing; counts once dimension_waiver_approved_by is set.

dimension_waiver_approved_by.description: Fact-only. The person who accepted dimension_waiver.

distinct_from.description: Keys this subject or value fact was checked to differ from; silences subject-duplicate and quantity-duplicate.

examples.description: Optional ground-term examples for a predicate schema.

exempts_claims.description: Requirement-only: claim keys of the exempted requirement this exception waives; omit to waive all of it.

fact_kind.description: Optional fact lane: subject, property_value, observation, meta, predicate_schema or predicate.

failure_side_waiver.description: Requirement-only: why the requirement has no failure side to test; counts once failure_side_waiver_approved_by is set.

failure_side_waiver_approved_by.description: Requirement-only. The person who accepted failure_side_waiver.

firmness.description: req/adr only: firm (a human's rule, needs origin.ref), default or exploratory. Absent = default if an agent wrote it.

granularity_reason.description: Optional justification for a coarse file or module-level traceability link when narrower symbols exist.

key_arguments.description: predicate_schema only: argument names that determine the remaining arguments (a functional dependency).

kind_of.description: subject only: defined subject keys this subject is a kind of (a read-only review is a kind of review view).

logic_claims.description: Requirement-only: every atomic claim key kb_model mode analyze returned; each must be grounded by a linked fact.

operator.description: Optional comparison operator for property_value facts, e.g. eq, gt, matches (regex), includes, subset_of, excludes.

origin.description: Optional provenance: kind (human, agent, migration, import) and authority (ref, approved_by, recorded_at).

approved_by.description: The person who reviewed and approved this entity's content, not the approved_by of an exception requirement.

kind.description: Who authored the entity: human, agent, migration (backfilled by kibi migrate) or import.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 time the provenance was recorded.

ref.description: Source reference for the authored content: URL, document path, ticket, commit or conversation id.

pair_reviews.description: Requirement only: verdicts on related pairs whose unmodeled claims cannot be modeled. Model the claims first.

part_of.description: subject only: defined subject keys this subject is a part of.

polarity.description: Optional polarity for property_value or predicate facts.

predicate_args.description: Optional ordered predicate arguments for ontology predicate facts; prefer kb_model mode predicates.

predicate_name.description: Optional predicate name for ontology predicate facts; prefer kb_model mode predicates.

predicate_namespace.description: Optional namespace for a project-local predicate schema.

proof_bindings.description: test only: native-runner bindings (symbol_id, target) for proof obligations; a rejection returns the full schema.

proof_contract.description: test only: kibi.proof-contract.v1 for this test; load the kibi-usage resource `proof` first. Rejections give the schema.

proof_receipts.description: test only: proof receipts kb_ingest_proof derives; never hand-write them. Send the stored list unchanged or omit it.

property_key.description: Optional snake_case property key for property_value facts. Example: 'session.timeout_minutes'.

rationale.description: Requirement-only: why it exists, in the stater's words; send it in the same write when they gave one, never invent one.

required_evidence.description: Requirement-only: weakest evidence level it accepts. Absent = tested if firm, else unverified.

rule_ir.description: Schema-validated kibi.logic.v1 rule IR. It is persisted as data and never executed as caller-supplied Prolog.

rule_schema_id.description: Rule schema fact ID used to validate this rule.

scope.description: Optional scope qualifier for fact entities.

semantic_clauses.description: Optional reviewed atomic decomposition of the prose, used when automatic sentence splitting needs an override.

semantic_inventory.description: Requirement proposition ledger from kb_model mode analyze; preserve entries while modeling each span.

semantic_inventory_version.description: Requirement-only proposition ledger contract version returned by kb_model mode analyze (CLI: kibi model).

semantic_key.description: Canonical semantic identity of the normalized logical model.

semantic_source_field.description: Requirement field whose exact UTF-8 bytes anchor semantic_inventory spans.

semantic_source_hash.description: SHA-256 of the exact semantic source text returned in the advisor inventory contract.

semantic_text.description: Requirement-only authored prose used for semantic inventory hashes and UTF-8 spans.

source.description: Optional provenance string. Example: '.kb/requirements/REQ-cli-gc.md'. Defaults to 'mcp://kibi/upsert'.

sourceFile.description: Optional code source file for symbol entities. Example: 'src/auth/login.ts'.

status.description: Required lifecycle state; allowed values depend on the entity type. Examples: 'open', 'passing', 'accepted'.

subject_key.description: Optional snake_case subject key for strict fact entities. Example: 'user.session'.

symbol_role.description: Optional role classification for symbol entities. Example: 'behavioral'.

title.description: Required short title. Example: 'Protect account settings endpoint'.

unit.description: Optional unit for numeric property_value facts.

value_bool.description: Optional boolean value for property_value facts.

value_int.description: Optional integer value for property_value facts.

value_number.description: Optional number value for property_value facts.

value_set.description: Optional exact set of values for property_value facts with value_type set, such as the members a domain must have.

value_string.description: Optional string value for property_value facts.

value_type.description: Optional value type for property_value facts; pair with exactly one value_string, _int, _number, _bool or _set.

verification_perspective.description: Optional typed verification perspective for test entities. Example: 'consumer'.

verification_scope.description: Optional typed verification scope for test entities. Example: 'end_to_end'.

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).
Entity type to create/update. Allowed: req, scenario, test, adr, flag, event, symbol, fact. Example: 'req'.

why.description: req only: why it exists, in the asker's words.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tool.name: kb_upsert
